title: Handling User Interactions
description: React to clicks, input events, and more with v-on and methods.

slides.title: Listening to Events with v-on
slides.content:
To make your app interactive, use `v-on` to listen to DOM events:

```html
<button v-on:click="methodName">Click me</button>
```

**Shorthand**: `@click="methodName"`

You can also pass arguments and access the event object:

```html
<button @click="greet('Hello', $event)">Say hi</button>
```

slides.title: Event Modifiers
slides.content:
Vue provides **event modifiers** to simplify common tasks:

- `.stop` – stops propagation
- `.prevent` – prevents default behavior
- `.once` – triggers only once

Example:
```html
<form @submit.prevent="onSubmit">...</form>
```

quizData.question: What is the shorthand for `v-on:click`?
quizData.explanation: `@click` is the shorthand for `v-on:click`. The `@` symbol represents 'on'.
